$comment: Solution profile: category-level, vendor-agnostic knowledge the agent layer retrieves when designing motions. Human-curated. Never a source of invented numbers — economics are ranges to be validated with customer data.
name: Infrastructure Automation
definition: Platforms and tooling that automate provisioning, configuration, orchestration, and day-2 operations across servers, networks, cloud, and hybrid infrastructure.
value_drivers: Reduce manual provisioning and configuration effort
Consistency and drift elimination across hybrid environments
Faster incident remediation and self-healing operations
Compliance and security policy enforced as code
Accelerate cloud migration and virtualization-exit programs
Free scarce senior engineers from repetitive work
competitive_conditions: Legacy job schedulers and runbook tooling
Point automation locked inside a single vendor stack
Competing platform team building on raw IaC only
common_triggers: Audit or compliance findings on configuration drift
M&A integration of divergent infrastructure estates
qualification_criteria: Named infrastructure or platform engineering leadership
Active modernization, migration, or cost initiative
Existing virtualization, container, or multi-cloud footprint

typical_economics.$comment: Ranges only; cite when used and validate with customer data.
typical_economics.deal_size_band: mid five to low seven figures depending on estate size
typical_economics.expansion_path: start with one automation domain, expand to network/security/ITSM automation

discovery_questions: How many distinct teams provision or change infrastructure today, and with what tooling?
What does your virtualization renewal timeline and cost trajectory look like?
Where does configuration drift or manual toil create incidents or audit findings?
What is the platform engineering team's mandate over the next 12 months?
Which workloads are moving (cloud, containers), and what automates that path today?
